# id: # Sweep S15 (scheduling boundaries and the menu), group C — the registry-op
# COMPLETIONS (BUG-152's post-op class, `ChoiceSite.postOp`): every op that
# wakes or releases a partner, followed by the issuer's private print beside
# the partner's print. Lane sweep/s15-scheduling, 2026-10-27, per the
# Neighbourhood line). Each set certified by coverage-observations at width 4;
# gc go1.26.5 sampled 100 plain / 100 -race / 30 at GOMAXPROCS=1 under the
# runners' pins, every draw a member.

subject: unbufferedPairPrints
why: an UNBUFFERED send pairs with the parked receiver (or parks until it arrives); after the pairing the sender's S and the receiver's R are concurrent through the post-op flag on each side: certified set {RS, SR} (members=2)

subject: recvThenPrint
why: a receive completion opens the post-op flag; the receiver's R and the sender's later S are concurrent: certified set {RS, SR} (members=2)

subject: closeWakePrints
why: close wakes the parked receiver; the closer's C and the woken receiver's R are concurrent: certified set {CR, RC} (members=2)

subject: selectCommitSendPrints
why: a select whose SEND clause commits is a registry-op completion (post-op flag); the sender's S and the receiver's R are concurrent: certified set {RS, SR} (members=2)

subject: selectCommitRecvPrints
why: a select whose RECEIVE clause commits is a registry-op completion; R and the sender's S are concurrent: certified set {RS, SR} (members=2)

subject: selectDefaultPrints
why: a select that takes its default completes no registry op (no post-op flag); the print after it is the next scheduling point, so D and the child's B are concurrent: certified set {BD, DB} (members=2) — X (the receive clause) is never a member, nobody sends

subject: selectWakePrints
why: a select that parks on its receive clause and is woken by the child's send, or commits at entry if the send came first; R and the sender's S are concurrent either way: certified set {RS, SR} (members=2)

subject: unlockWakePrints
why: Unlock releases the parked locker (or the child locks uncontended later); the unlocker's U and the locker's L are concurrent: certified set {LU, UL} (members=2)

subject: doneWakePrints
why: Done wakes Wait; the Done goroutine's D and main's W after Wait are concurrent: certified set {DW, WD} (members=2)

subject: onceWakePrints
why: two callers of one Once: F runs exactly once before either caller's own print (the second caller parks in its Do until the first completes, or finds it done); A and B are concurrent: certified set {FAB, FBA} (members=2)

subject: runlockWakeWriterPrints
why: RUnlock releases the pending writer; the reader's R and the writer's W are concurrent: certified set {RW, WR} (members=2)

subject: atomicThenPrint
why: an atomic Add (the typed wrapper) completes on each side with the post-op flag; the prints after them are concurrent and the sum after the join is 11 on every schedule: certified set {MS 11, SM 11} (members=2)

subject: recoveredSendClosedPrints
why: a send on a closed channel panics (no post-op flag opens on an unwinding successor) and is recovered; the print after the recovery is the next scheduling point, so A and the child's B are concurrent: certified set {AB, BA} (members=2)
